plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds send up slender spikes crowded with fragrant violet-blue flowers. In late July the fields hum with bees, and the warm air smells sweet and herbal.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer, with peak bloom from late June through July and into early August
plants.location: Provence, France, and lavender fields across southern Europe
plants.funFact: The name lavender probably comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Tall stems carry broad golden-rayed flower heads that turn to follow the sun while they are young. Whole fields of them glow across the summer countryside.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn, with peak bloom from July to August
plants.location: Northern Hemisphere farmland and gardens, including the Great Plains of the United States and southern and central Europe
plants.funFact: Each sunflower head is a cluster of hundreds to thousands of tiny individual florets. The seeds form in a spiral pattern that follows the Fibonacci sequence.

plants.name: Epilobium angustifolium
plants.description: Tall spires of bright magenta-pink flowers open from the bottom up. They blaze across mountain meadows, roadsides and burned forest clearings.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer, roughly July to September, with peak bloom in July and August at northern latitudes
plants.location: Alaska, Canada, the Rocky Mountains and northern Europe
plants.funFact: Fireweed is among the first plants to colonize land after a wildfire. Its flowers open progressively up the stalk, which gives rise to the saying that summer is nearly over when the blooms reach the top.
